issues.problem: The source-family rule can be read as a closed-set holdout protocol for the only two original 0/1 glyphs. With all variants of each original kept together, a nonempty holdout of either sole source also holds out that entire character class. This differs from the actual 0-99 experiment, which holds out full digit strings but reuses familiar character classes and one fixed font. The text needs to identify these units and their test questions explicitly.
issues.impact: Readers may conflate unseen source images or unseen classes with unseen strings assembled from familiar character glyphs; the correct 2/30 cannot resolve that distinction.
issues.verified_parts: Identity-preserving variants keep intended labels; dependent variants should stay together for the selected unseen-source-group test; existing raw 2/30 and all numeric/figure checks remain verified. No actual experiment family overlap or class-leakage defect was found.
issues.suggested_resolution: State that the two 0/1 fixtures only demonstrate pixel-label pairing, and that holding out a sole per-class source also holds out a class. For evaluating new source images of known classes, obtain multiple independent originals per class and keep source variants together. Explicitly state the 0-99 experiment groups each complete digit string with its three offsets, training already contains 0-9, and the holdout tests new whole strings in the same font, not new character classes or new fonts.
